config.grain_rationale: One record is one charity as registered with the ACNC, i.e. one legal entity holding charity registration. The address columns are the charity's contact address, not a site or premises record, and the operational and purpose flag columns are attributes of that same registered entity. Record identity is therefore the entity.

record_id.rationale: ABN was tried first but the full register contains 6 holdout records that collide on ABN: the register includes related/sub-entity rows and rows with no ABN, so ABN is not a unique per-record key across the whole file even though it looked unique in discovery (477 of 477 distinct in 480 rows). content_hash is used instead so every distinct row gets a traceable, stable id without inventing uniqueness. ABN remains mapped as entity.abn where present.

fields.rationale: Column labelled ABN; 477/477 present values are 11 digits with a valid ABN checksum (abn_checksum_valid_rate 1.0), and 0 errors on holdout. Canonical Australian business identifier. Note the same ABN can appear on more than one row, so it is not used as the record id.

Column is explicitly Charity_Legal_Name and the publisher states the register presents the formal legal name. Scope current_legal_name. Held-out values carry legal-form suffixes (Incorporated, 'The Trustee for ...', 'P&C Association'), consistent with registered names rather than display names. The source gives no start date for the name itself, so no valid_from_path; Registration_Date is deliberately not attached to the name.

Publisher evidence states the effective registration date is the date with ACNC, explicitly distinguished from the organisation's original establishment. 476/480 discovery values and 1179/1179 holdout values match dd/mm/yyyy (0 errors). The date is when ACNC charity registration became true, hence scope charity_registration and valid_from_path on this claim.

Column is the charity's website; values are bare domains (www.x.org.au) or http(s) URLs. The website op rejects malformed values. One holdout value is prose containing two URLs and a parenthetical ('HTTPS://... AND WWW... (WWWW...)') rather than a single URL; rejecting that is the correct outcome, since coercing it would emit a broken URL as the entity's canonical website.

Three free-text street lines of the charity's contact address, joined with a single space so multi-line addresses cannot concatenate without a separator; lines 2 and 3 are almost always null so the separator rarely appears. Publisher evidence says the address is contact information, hence scope entity_contact_address. Caveat a reviewer should know: Address_Line_1 often holds a venue/premises or building descriptor rather than a street line (e.g. 'Pembroke School', 'St Christopher's Pastoral Centre', 'Egan Park', 'Community Centre') alongside true street addresses, and some values are PO boxes. The source does not distinguish a licensed/operating premises address from the entity's contact address, so this is mapped as contact_address and not as a premises address; downstream users should not treat address.full as a verified street address.

Town_City is the suburb/locality of the contact address; 362 distinct discovery values and all 1061 holdout values read as Australian localities ('Dubbo', 'Altona North', 'DONNYBROOK'), published case preserved as no canonical casing rule exists.

State column holds AU state/territory abbreviations; holdout includes a trailing-whitespace value ('SA ') which trim then state resolves to SA. state sends anything unrecognised to OTHER rather than guessing. 0 errors on holdout.

Postcode is the contact address postcode; the postcode op validates 4-digit AU codes and re-pads 3-digit NT codes. The column is free text and carries occasional junk rather than just formatting noise: holdout rejects were '80571' (5 digits) and 'Cloverdale' (a locality name entered in the postcode field), plus one 6-digit value in discovery. Rejecting these is correct behaviour because coercing a locality name or a 5-digit string into address.postcode would assert a postcode the source never stated; the loss is a fraction of a percent of rows.

Country of the contact address. Discovery shows only 'Australia' in mixed case plus one 'Singapore'. The previous passthrough behaviour asserted any unrecognised string as a canonical country, which turned a publisher typo ('Austria' on an Altona North VIC contact address) into a false country claim. passthrough is now false: only explicitly recognised values are emitted (Australian spellings -> AU, Singapore -> SG because the source genuinely states it) and anything else is left unmapped rather than asserted. Residual uncertainty: an unlisted genuine overseas country would be dropped rather than emitted.

unmapped.reason: The critic suggested a filtered emission to entity.trading_name, and some holdout values do look like public names ('Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.', 'Walker Close Community Centre'). I am still leaving it unmapped. Publisher evidence states this column is the names the charity is publicly known by and explicitly does NOT classify every alternate name as a trading name, so emitting trading_name would assert a trading use the source does not establish. The column is also irreducibly heterogeneous: person names ('Shannon Schedlich'), fragments ('Admin', 'NSP'), legal-form-tweaked duplicates of the legal name itself ('Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.' vs 'Donnybrook Mens Shed Incorporated' - a spelling variant, not a trading name), and trust-entity wrappers. A filter cannot separate spelling variants from genuine trading names without guesswork. If this is wanted downstream it should be modelled as an alias/other-name field, not entity.trading_name.

Constant 'Business' on 480/480 rows; describes the category of the address record, not a canonical entity attribute. Address semantics are already carried by the address.* mappings, and mapping it to entity_type would be a guess.
Count of the charity's responsible persons (officers); an attribute of governance, not of the entity's identity, form or status. No ontology target.
Accounting period end (e.g. '30-Jun') is a reporting convention, not a date of the entity or of a claim in the ontology.

Comma-separated ISO country codes of countries where the charity operates, not where it is located. address.country is the entity's own address country, so mapping this would be a false location claim. No ontology target for operational reach.
Private Benevolent Institution tax concession flag; a tax status of the charity, not entity.status (which is registration/liquidation state) and not entity_type.
Health Promotion Charity tax concession flag; same reasoning as PBI.
Beneficiary-group flag; describes who the charity serves, not the entity's own attributes.

config.notes: REVISION after holdout review. Changes: (1) record_id switched from columns[ABN] to content_hash - the error was real, 6 holdout rows collide on ABN because the register contains related/sub-entity rows and rows lacking an ABN. (2) address.country passthrough disabled - the previous passthrough emitted a typo ('Austria' on an Altona North VIC address) as an asserted canonical country; now only explicitly recognised values emit (AU, and SG for the Singapore rows actually present). (3) Rejected WEBSITE_INVALID and POSTCODE_INVALID values are intentional rejections of malformed prose / locality-names-in-postcode, not parser bugs; documented in their rationales. (4) address.full confidence lowered to 0.72 and its rationale now warns that the first line is often a venue/premises or PO box descriptor rather than a street address. (5) Other_Organisation_Names remains unmapped despite the critic's 'missed' suggestion: publisher evidence warns alternate names are not attested trading names, and the column mixes spelling variants of the legal name with person names and fragments, so a filter would require guesswork; the correct model is an alias field. (6) Date_Organisation_Established is a genuine ontology gap (no entity.date_established). No entity.status or entity.entity_type mapping was added: the register has no deregistered/in-liquidation or business-form column, so both stay unasserted rather than guessed.

fields.reason: Charity_Size holds the ACNC reporting-size class (Small/Medium/Large) and maps one-to-one to context.charity.size; null and 'NOT APPLICABLE' correctly emit nothing, and the held-out rows show 'Small' emitted and blank rows emitted nothing.

Date_Organisation_Established is parsed as %d/%m/%Y; the held-out rows confirm day/month order (05/09/2023 -> 2023-09-05, 31/12/1889 -> 1889-12-31, 13/11/2006 -> 2006-11-13), which would be impossible under month-first parsing. The publisher evidence states this is the original establishment date, distinct from registration, matching the ontology note. Blank/null correctly emits nothing.
This rule maps the Y flag for preventing or relieving animal suffering to the Animal welfare purpose; the mapping is direct and blank or N values emit nothing.
The Advancing_Culture Y flag corresponds exactly to the Culture enum; the held-out record shows only that one purpose emitted.
The Advancing_Education Y flag corresponds to the Education enum; a held-out row confirms it.
The Advancing_Health Y flag corresponds to the Health enum; held-out rows confirm it.

The flag for promoting or opposing a change to law, government policy or practice corresponds to Public policy and advocacy; the mapping is semantically direct and does not depend on unknown enum values.
The source column name contains a typo, but the column Advancing_natual_environment clearly means advancing the natural environment, so the label 'Natural environment' is correct.
The flag for promoting or protecting human rights corresponds to the Human rights enum.
The 'other analogous purposes beneficial to the general public' flag corresponds to General public benefit; the source typo does not change the meaning.
The flag for promoting reconciliation, mutual respect and tolerance corresponds exactly to Reconciliation and tolerance.
The Advancing_Religion Y flag corresponds to the Religion enum; several held-out rows confirm it.
The flag for advancing social or public welfare corresponds to Social and public welfare; held-out rows confirm it.
The flag for advancing the security or safety of Australia or the Australian public corresponds to Public safety.
Operates_in_ACT reflects the operating jurisdiction, so emitting ACT is consistent with the ontology's service-footprint semantics; the held-out record confirms it.
Operates_in_NSW corresponds to NSW; held-out rows confirm it.
Operates_in_NT corresponds to NT; the held-out all-states record confirms it.
Operates_in_QLD corresponds to QLD; held-out rows confirm it.
Operates_in_SA corresponds to SA; held-out rows confirm it.
Operates_in_TAS corresponds to TAS; the held-out all-states record confirms it.
Operates_in_VIC corresponds to VIC; held-out rows confirm it.
Operates_in_WA corresponds to WA; held-out rows confirm it.

critic.summary: All 22 rules are acceptable. Size maps the source's own reporting-size class, and the date parse is verifiably day/month (31/12/1889, 13/11/2006), aligned with the publisher's distinction between establishment and registration. Every purpose flag maps to a semantically matching enum and emits only on affirmative values. Every operating-region flag maps to the corresponding jurisdiction as a service footprint rather than an address. Blank and negative flags correctly emit nothing, and each emitted value is correctly typed. Nothing material was left unmapped: unmapped columns are beneficiary-group flags, tax-concession flags, officer counts, accounting dates, operating-country reach, a constant address category, and the heterogeneous Other_Organisation_Names column; the mapping is right to withhold trading_name there, because publisher evidence says alternate names are not classified as trading names.
